question: Should tools.exec.denylist be an operator guardrail that overrides ordinary full/off execution but remains bypassable by an explicitly authorized elevated-full run?
rationale: The diff changes a privileged execution boundary and introduces a new configuration contract; source correctness cannot determine whether elevated-full is intentionally stronger than an operator STOP rule.

options.title: Approve guardrail semantics
options.body: Keep elevated-full as the explicit break-glass bypass, correct the configuration documentation, and require exact-head integrated companion proof before merge.

options.title: Make STOP rules absolute
options.body: Apply denylist review requirements to elevated-full execution as well, updating implementation, tests, help text, and runtime proof.

options.title: Decline the new policy surface
options.body: Close or substantially narrow the PR if maintainers do not want another exec configuration and approval-precedence contract.

recommendation.title: Approve guardrail semantics
recommendation.body: Keep elevated-full as the explicit break-glass bypass, correct the configuration documentation, and require exact-head integrated companion proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion and adjacent exec-approval security work identify steipete as the strongest available owner for this boundary decision.
